title: Week 5 of letting an AI agent trade ZEC: beat BTC, lost to just holding ZEC
author: ruby-cos
selftext:
Running a trend-following agent (EMA 12/26, 4h) on ZEC with $500 of simulated money. 

After five weeks: +9.45%, max drawdown 6.84%, 7 closed trades plus one open short, fees about $0.52. For reference, BTC is up roughly 4% over the same period. 

It only puts about 20% of the account into each trade, so most of the capital sits in cash by design. On that roughly $100 per trade, the agent made about $46 (including the open short). Holding $100 of ZEC over the same stretch would have made about $26. Measured against the full $500, simply holding ZEC (up roughly 26%) would have beaten it. Position size is adjustable, so a more aggressive setting would change these numbers a lot, in both directions.

Small sample, simulated money. I’ll keep tracking it.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: losing to just holding ZEC is the useful result here. 7 closed trades in five weeks is too few to say much, but a trend filter that trails buy and hold in a trending coin usually keeps trailing it.

comments.author: DatGiantIsopod
comments.body: Imo the "beaten by hold" metric is pointless because it assumes that you'd magically know the top of the market to sell and thus "beat" your bot. "Beaten by hold" isn't really what the coin did, it would actually be an entire different strategy that can predict the local top so you could actually profit from that move. A successful trading strategy, agentic or otherwise, locks in profit as it goes along and is agnostic about a coin's performance.
